Hi Jane,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you and the security team. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key items and next steps so we have a shared reference.

Recap (high level):
- Scope: Private/VPC deployment for production inference (no customer data to Redwood-hosted public endpoints).
- Data types: Customer will send PHI/PII in requests (clinical notes + identifiers) — this is a mandatory design constraint.
- Retention: AcmeHealth requires request/response retention <= 30 days for troubleshooting; logs beyond that must be redacted/anonymized.
- Logging: Access/audit logs and request tracing required; no raw PII in long-term logs.
- Residency: Primary deployment in us-east-1; must ensure egress controls block unintended outbound traffic.
- On-prem/air-gapped: Evaluating on-prem package; need to surface constraints early.

Action items / next steps:
1) Acme to share current VPC network diagram and egress policy (we discussed privately attaching). Jane — can you send the diagram and any firewall rules?
2) Technical deep-dive: Dev to run through port/endpoint requirements and logging configuration. We suggested a 1-hour session next week.
3) We will provide a short checklist for required firewall rules, minimal ports, and our recommended encryption + KMS flow.
4) Draft MAP (mutual action plan) and timeline for a Private deployment proof-of-concept. Rishi will own commercial/exec alignment.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_cheatsheet.pdf (quick checklist).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling for the technical deep-dive.

Jane / Marissa — following up with technical details ahead of the deep-dive (so we can use time for any edge cases):

1) Logging & PII:
- Production Private deployments run with a customer-configurable logging profile. By default, request/response payloads are NOT persisted to long-term logs. We keep ephemeral tracing (in-memory) for up to 72 hours for debugging, which can be reduced to 0 hours on request.
- Access/audit logs (who/when) are recorded without including raw request payloads. For troubleshooting flows where payload inspection is required, we support short-lived, encrypted debugging packages that can be enabled per-session and are automatically purged after the agreed retention window (we can set this to 30 days or fewer).
- We support field-level redaction via a ruleset at the edge so that PII elements (SSNs, names depending on config) can be stripped before any logs are created.

2) Egress & control plane:
- For our Private VPC offering (non-air-gapped) the control plane needs to reach our management endpoints for telemetry, license checks, and software updates. These can be routed through Acme's NAT/Proxy and whitelisted IP ranges.
- For air-gapped/on-prem options, we provide an on-prem appliance bundle: full offline install, manual patching process, and local KMS integration. This option removes outbound requirements but adds a slightly longer provisioning timeline and additional support SLAs.

3) Network ports & minimal requirements (recommendation):
- Outbound HTTPS (443) to our control-plane IP ranges (we will provide the list) for management (if not air-gapped).
- Ports for internal health checks between nodes (TCP 9000-9010) — allowed within VPC only.
- SSH access restricted to jump hosts for initial install (optional; installs can be done via automation).

4) Data residency & encryption:
- All data at rest encrypted using customer-managed KMS if required.
- Models/text in KV caches are encrypted in memory and on-disk; caches can be configured not to persist to disk.

I’ve attached a short security checklist (redwood_vpc_security_checklist.pdf) that maps to SOC 2 controls and the items you suggested. Let me know what time works for the technical deep-dive — mornings PST generally work for our infra team.

Thanks,
